clue.text: Preferred getting temperature inside pastry dish, using measuring device

indicators.note: the pastry dish has the other pieces put inside it, so it is opened up to hold them
the pastry dish has the other pieces put inside it, so it is opened up to hold them

parts.note: a pie is a dish baked in pastry
a pet project or pet subject is a preferred one

explanation.surface: A cook measures out ingredients for a favourite pie at just the right temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: A laboratory tube for drawing up and dispensing exact small volumes of liquid is a measuring device.

clue.text: Cycle a bit, over a great distance, before night comes round

indicators.note: before puts the earlier pieces ahead of the final one

parts.note: a penny is a small coin, a little bit of money
far means over a great distance

indicators.note: the word night comes round into a new order of its letters

parts.note: taken as written before reshuffling

explanation.surface: A cyclist rides a little way, then a long way, as night closes in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycle' looks like a verb, but it is a noun: the old high-wheeled bicycle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian bicycle with one huge front wheel and a tiny rear one is a cycle, named after two old British coins of differing size.

clue.text: European river leads to another river, northwards, and another river

parts.note: the Po is the great river of northern Italy
something that leads to a place goes to it, giving to

indicators.note: in a down clue, going northwards means reading upwards, so the river name is reversed

parts.note: the Cam flows through Cambridge

explanation.surface: A geography note tracing one European river into a chain of others.
explanation.definitionFit: The Potomac flows past Washington DC, so it is yet one more river in the list.

clue.text: In fact, make an effort to tour centre of Toulon

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the attempt word goes round the inner letters

parts.note: to try is to make an effort

indicators.note: the central letters of the six-letter Toulon are taken

explanation.surface: A traveller resolves to try a trip around the middle of the French port of Toulon.
explanation.definitionFit: Truly and in fact are both adverbs asserting that something is genuinely so.

clue.text: Regal ground, during design, became bigger

indicators.note: during places the reworked letters within the purpose word

parts.note: a design is an aim or intention, an end

indicators.note: ground, as past tense of grind, means crushed into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something regal is ground up as part of a design process and it grows.
explanation.definitionFit: Enlarged is the past tense of a verb meaning grew in size, matching the past-tense phrase.

clue.text: Cry from group of players rejecting latest stage work

indicators.note: the final step of the word, its last letter, is thrown out

parts.note: a squad is a team of players
WK is a standard abbreviation for work

explanation.surface: A theatre company's protest at being refused the newest stage production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stage work' reads as a play, but 'stage' belongs with 'rejecting latest', the dropping of the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A squawk is a loud harsh cry, like that of an alarmed bird.

clue.text: Outstay, when retired, one's time away

indicators.note: retiring is withdrawing or going back, so the short form is read backwards

parts.note: one's taken as I'S, the letter I for one plus the S
out means away, as in not at home

explanation.surface: A pensioner overstays, spending their retirement time away from home.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit out something is to stay until it has ended, outlasting it.

clue.text: Hesitating private then breaks free — the last of many

parts.note: um is the sound of someone hesitating
PTE is the military abbreviation for private

indicators.note: the word then breaks loose into a new arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A soldier, after some hesitation, makes a break for freedom.
explanation.definitionFit: Umpteenth describes the latest in a long, unspecified series, the final one of a great many.

clue.text: American bird's torn into comic

indicators.note: into puts the ripped piece inside the joker

parts.note: a wit is a comic, someone funny
rent is an old past participle of rend, meaning torn

explanation.surface: A bird from America has been ripped into a comic strip.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of bird's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The wrentit is a small songbird of the western United States, so it is an American bird.

clue.text: Vegetarian food fanatic given mullet? It's allowed

parts.note: a nut is an enthusiast or fanatic
the mullet is a haircut, short at the front and long at the back, so a cut
to let is to allow; let as a verb gives permission

explanation.surface: A food fanatic offered fish asks whether it is permitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mullet?' suggests the fish, but it is the hairstyle, a kind of cut; the question mark flags the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutlet made from chopped nuts is a classic meat-free dish for those who avoid meat.

clue.text: Religious art that is displayed in exercise area

indicators.note: the short form is shown inside the other letters

parts.note: PT is physical training, exercise

explanation.surface: Religious artwork is put on show in a gym.
explanation.definitionFit: A pietà is a painting or sculpture of the Virgin Mary holding the dead Christ, a religious artwork.

clue.text: Nick vacated lavatory in the correct way

parts.note: to nick is to steal, to appropriate

indicators.note: a vacated word is emptied of its middle, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone steals from a lavatory that has just been emptied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacated' leaves LY, the outer letters of lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Appropriately means in a fitting, suitable or proper manner.

clue.text: Delicious yoghurt Ursula made originally? I'm surprised

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of each of the three words

parts.note: my is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone tasting Ursula's home-made yoghurt is pleasantly surprised.
explanation.definitionFit: Yummy is informal for tasty or delicious.

clue.text: Type of march, unpopular in France, is described by holiday guide

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw round, so the guide goes around the other letters

parts.note: a holiday rep is a tour company's representative at a resort
out means out of favour, unpopular
est is French for is

explanation.surface: A holiday rep sums up a march that has fallen out of favour in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Route step is a marching style allowing troops to keep their own pace and talk, used on long marches.

clue.text: New cashier wraps first piece of vinyl in record store

indicators.note: wraps means goes around, so the reworked letters enclose the single letter
new suggests a fresh arrangement of the letters of cashier
the opening letter of vinyl is taken

explanation.surface: A new cashier at a record shop gift-wraps a vinyl LP.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges CASHIER into ARCHIES, which wraps round V.
explanation.definitionFit: Archives are a store of historical records, so a record store in another sense.

clue.text: Contribution from workers present on jet and chopper in US

parts.note: in means present, as in at home
the Comet was the first jet airliner
ax is the American spelling of axe, a chopper

explanation.surface: An American gift for workers arrives by jet and helicopter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopper' suggests a helicopter but means an axe, spelt AX in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: Tax levied on earnings is a payment that employed people make to the state.

clue.text: Footballers' move, say, went wrong in goalless match?

indicators.note: in puts the reworked letters within the scoreline

parts.note: a goalless match ends nil-nil, two zeros, read as two Os

indicators.note: wrong signals that the letters of went go awry

explanation.surface: A football move failed in a match that ended with no goals.
explanation.walkthrough: A goalless draw is 0-0, read as two letter Os.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-two is a quick exchange of passes between two players, a footballing move; 'say' marks it as an example.

clue.text: Mushroom I found during dig that will be eaten at Christmas?

definitions.text: that will be eaten at Christmas?

indicators.note: these pieces are found within the excavation word

parts.note: a mine is a dig, an excavation
the cep is an edible wild mushroom, the porcino

explanation.surface: An archaeologist turns up a mushroom on a dig and saves it for the Christmas table.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pastry filled with dried fruit and spice is traditional British festive fare in December.

clue.text: Material which covered houses primarily

parts.note: that and which are interchangeable relative pronouns

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, taking the leading letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A description of the material that once roofed houses.
explanation.walkthrough: Not quite &lit, but the wordplay describes the definition: straw or reed roofing that covered houses.
explanation.definitionFit: Straw or reeds used for roofing are a building material.

clue.text: Football club magazine

definitions.meaning: the London Premier League side known as the Gunners
a magazine is a store of arms and ammunition

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a store of weapons, which the Gunners of north London took as their football club's name.

clue.text: Bird and man audibly clash

indicators.note: audibly signals going by the sound of the chess word rather than its spelling

parts.note: a knight is a chess man, a playing piece
to jar is to clash, as colours or sounds do

explanation.surface: A man and a bird have a noisy confrontation.
explanation.walkthrough: In chess the pieces are called men, so the knight is a man.
explanation.definitionFit: The nightjar is a nocturnal bird with a churring call, active at dusk.

clue.text: First person in France seeing an insect, mostly green

parts.note: je is French for I, the first person singular
an is the indefinite article, a

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a louse is a parasitic insect

explanation.surface: The first French person to see a mostly green insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Green, as in green with envy, describes someone resentful of another's good fortune.

clue.text: Spot that woman's musical instrument

parts.note: a zit is a slang word for a spot or pimple
her is the possessive for that woman

explanation.surface: A spot on a woman's musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A stringed instrument with a flat soundbox, plucked while laid horizontally.

clue.text: One maybe needing number and coins, frantically, to ring Mina abroad

definitions.note: a number here is something that numbs, a sedative

indicators.note: ringing means encircling, so the first jumble goes around the second
frantically suggests wild disorder in the letters of coins
abroad means all over the place, scattering the letters of Mina

explanation.surface: Someone frantically gathers a phone number and coins to call Mina overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' looks like a figure but is read numb-er, a drug that numbs. 'frantically' makes INSOC and 'abroad' makes MNIA, which INSOC rings.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who cannot sleep may well need a sedative to dull their senses.

clue.text: It is retro gear, only half a crown

indicators.note: retro means backwards, so the word it is turned round
only half of the word gear is kept, its second pair of letters

explanation.surface: Vintage clothing that costs only half a crown, an old British coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half a crown' reads as the old British coin worth two shillings and sixpence, but 'a' joins the wordplay and 'crown' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A jewelled headband or coronet is a kind of crown.

clue.text: Pound found in bath robe

indicators.note: the letters are found within the two words

explanation.surface: A pound coin discovered in a dressing gown pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: To throb is to pound or beat heavily, like a pulse.

clue.text: Characters outside on Glenlivet, an alcoholic drink

indicators.note: the two end letters sit outside the joining word
the characters at the two ends of the whisky name are taken

parts.note: on means in addition, and

explanation.surface: A whisky drinker reflects on a Speyside single malt.
explanation.walkthrough: The outside characters of Glenlivet, a Scotch whisky, are G and T, which is the answer as said; the parse shows it as G, AND, T.
explanation.definitionFit: Gin and tonic is a popular mixed drink containing spirits.

clue.text: Basil perhaps sustains yelp peripherally, a cry of approval for rhetorical figure

indicators.note: to sustain is to hold up or support, so the herb holds the edge letters within it

parts.note: basil is an example of a herb

indicators.note: peripherally means at the edges, so the outer letters of yelp

parts.note: olé is the cry of approval at a bullfight

explanation.surface: A man named Basil keeps yelping in approval of a speaker's fine phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Basil' looks like a man's name but is the herb; HERB holds YP, the outer letters of yelp.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyperbole is deliberate exaggeration, a figure of speech used for effect.

clue.text: About 59, semi-pro regularly appeared, needing invigorating substance

indicators.note: about means around, so the alternate letters go around the Roman number
regularly takes every other letter of semi-pro

parts.note: LIX is 59 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A semi-professional player turned up regularly at about the age of 59, needing a tonic.
explanation.definitionFit: An elixir is a magical or medicinal potion believed to restore vigour or prolong life.

clue.text: Diplomatic office getting space — it could be fishy

parts.note: an em is a unit of space in printing
bassy means deep-toned, but read as like a bass, the fish, it is fishy

explanation.surface: An office is given more room, though something smells suspicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fishy' suggests suspicious, but here it means like a bass, the fish: BASSY.
explanation.definitionFit: An embassy is the official residence or office of an ambassador abroad.
